text:
Cutter Gauthier is having the kind of month people will look up later. After his goal against San Jose on Tuesday, Daily Faceoff counted 19 in November, one shy of the NHL record for a single month, and Hockey.com noted he had become the first American to score 21 goals in 14 games. He has 14 points in his last 10, and he is our likeliest scorer on the ice tonight at 41%. Our numbers also flag him as due to cool, which is the polite way of saying nobody keeps this pace.

The trouble for Anaheim is that Gauthier's month has come alongside a 1-4-0 week. The Ducks lost 5-3 at home to these same Kings last night after leading by two, and the replays said they deserved more: they won 56% of the simulations of that game's shots. They are playing without Leo Carlsson, now on injured reserve with 29 points in 24 games, and Ryan Poehling. Lukas Dostal, projected in net, is at minus 6.8 goals saved above expected, and that has been the leak all season.

Los Angeles is 4-1-0 in its last five without driving much of the play, winning the chance battle in just one of those games. Artemi Panarin is back from injury and is our pick of either team for two points at 36%. Anton Forsberg gets the start over Darcy Kuemper, who has taken 14 of the 23. Drew Doughty played his 1,300th game with the Kings this week, which is the kind of number that only a few defensemen in league history have reached with one team.

Both teams flew nowhere: it is the second night of a back-to-back, the same two rosters, and one night's worth of grudges. Beckett Sennecke has six points in five career games against the Kings, and Alex Laferriere, he of the between-the-legs goal this week, is one of our Sleepers at 56% for a point.
headline: Gauthier's November gets one more Kings rematch
